title: Fan-out bound comment overclaims: bound caps parallel sending drafts at 3, not emails at 3/recipient/hour
evidence:
-- (max 3 continue emails per recipient per hour across ALL vacancies: the
-- endpoint is public, so without this an attacker sprays branded Resend
-- email at a victim from many vacancies). The handler answers 200 without
-- sending in every zero-row case.
...
  AND (
    SELECT count(*) FROM application_draft d2
    WHERE d2.email = lower($2)
      AND d2.last_link_sent_at IS NOT NULL
      AND d2.last_link_sent_at > now() - interval '1 hour'
  ) < 3
detail: The subquery counts draft ROWS whose latest send stamp is within the hour, not sends. A single draft resends every 10 min (count=1<3 forever, ~6 emails/hr); two drafts sustain ~12/hr. Only cross-draft parallelism is capped at 3.
recommended_fix: Reword the comment to state the real bound (max 3 distinct drafts sending per hour, each separately 10-min cooldown-limited), or implement a true per-recipient hourly send counter.

title: Resume GET and draft save/continue-link gates skip the max_applications cap the pristine form GET enforces
detail: handle_get_form (application_handler.gleam:64) shows the closed page when check_max_applications trips, but handle_resume and lookup_accepting_vacancy only check status/archived/expiry — a draft holder on a full vacancy gets a resumable form that refuses at submit; saves keep flowing.
recommended_fix: Mirror check_max_applications in handle_resume and lookup_accepting_vacancy so capped vacancies render the closed page / refuse draft writes up front, matching the pristine GET and POST gates.

title: 500-draft cap refusal returns ok:true though nothing was persisted, and the client treats it as acknowledged
detail: upsert_application_draft returns zero rows for both the deliberate tombstone/submitted no-op AND a new pair refused by the 500-cap; Ok(_) answers ok:true for both, so form_draft.js sets lastSentPayload (beacon won't retry) and fires application_draft_saved for a write that never happened.
recommended_fix: Distinguish the cap refusal (pre-count or a RETURNING reason column) and answer ok:false; the cap is vacancy-wide, not email-specific, so signalling it leaks nothing the anti-oracle design protects.

title: Five new form_copy draft constants are unreferenced; JS sync rests on a comment and a substring-only JS test
detail: Grep shows no Gleam reference to draft_prep_note/draft_continue_button/draft_continue_sent/draft_continue_needs_email/draft_continue_failed (only a doc comment at form_view.gleam:124); form_draft.test.js pins only substrings of the JS copies, so drift between the two would be silent.
recommended_fix: Pin equality: add a Gleam test reading priv/static/form_draft.js and asserting it contains each form_copy constant, or drop the unreferenced Gleam constants and keep the strings JS-side only.

title: validate_body_size docstring still claims the strict CL/TE arms apply only to /apply/* POSTs
detail: The diff arms the F3 draft writes with the same strict rules (CL required, TE rejected, 64 KB cap) and updated evaluate_body_size's docstring accordingly, but this adjacent docstring still says the refusal affects no other route.
recommended_fix: Update the validate_body_size docstring to mention the draft-write strict arms and the 64 KB max_draft_body_size cap, mirroring the evaluate_body_size doc.

title: tracked_application_url docstring's fixed template-slug list omits the two slugs this PR adds
detail: The PR adds tracked_application_url callers with "application_draft_continue" (build_continue_draft_html) and "application_reminder_2_continue" (build_reminder_stage2_html), but the docstring still presents the four pre-F3 slugs as the fixed set.
recommended_fix: Add "application_draft_continue" and "application_reminder_2_continue" to the slug list in the tracked_application_url docstring.
